result.choiceRationale: R-P5 is the most closable candidate: mechanism selection is largely complete, both mechanisms survived selected physical attacks, and the remaining work is final acceptance gates, commit, and structured self-release. This is a near-terminal closeout that converts an existing verified mechanism into a graduated production state — a concrete frontier delta (owner-mechanism-change) with minimal residual uncertainty. G-AF3 is high-value (generalization testing) but is the start of a new multi-variant experiment with substantial design cost and no guarantee of clean separation of surviving priors from overfit. HOST-PKG is a packaging/import-graph audit whose value is conditional on whether a narrower surface is even justified (ambiguity-reduction at best). H-P6 is externally blocked on DeepSeek DNS recovery — the control-path repair is causally admitted but live experiments cannot run now. F-C2-BLOCKED is a negative control with a dominant external admission blocker (no independent Linux/systemd host exists); it should be deferred, not funded.
result.predictedDiscriminator: Whether R-P5's final portable/physical gates pass cleanly, enabling the fast-forward and structured self-release to graduate production.
result.selectionFalsifier: If R-P5's final portable or physical acceptance gates reveal a previously-unseen defect requiring mechanism re-selection (rather than a trivial fix), then the closeout was not as terminal as assumed and G-AF3's generalization experiment would have been the better marginal investment.
